notes: Consensus explicitly acknowledges weak comparative evidence and allows individualized practice; not an evidence-graded operative algorithm.
Physical ISL stages0–III are explicitly defined for extremities; direct genital staging/percentage-volume extrapolation must be qualified.
CDT phase1 reduction and phase2 maintenance; no universal required weeks or genital pressure range. Pneumatic treatment can displace edema into genitalia/proximally; individualized monitoring.
Surgery selection and imaging depend on actual functional vessels, tissue composition and context; early-stage success generalization is chiefly extremity experience.
VLNT donor lymphedema reported; reverse mapping may reduce, not eliminate risk. Combined scar release/compression confounds outcomes.

Excision can serve advanced genital disease; superficial collateral loss, wound problems and recurrence considered. Charles/Thompson approaches generally discouraged when alternatives available; this is not a ban on all modern tailored genital excision.

Specialized liposuction is established for selected nonpitting extremity lymphedema, distinct from cosmetic liposuction; long-term compression remains essential. Do not infer equivalent established genital benefit from limb evidence.
Omental transposition/enteromesenteric bridges described as unproven and discouraged; distinguish this from contemporary vascularized omental node transfer, which is a different operation.
Long-term diuretics discouraged for pure lymphedema; comorbid conditions can justify them. MLD additive volume evidence primarily breast-cancer limbs, not genital cohorts.
